question: What type of rays are a significant hazard during arc welding?
solution:
The correct answer is __Ultraviolet and infrared rays**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ultraviolet (UV) and infrared (IR) rays__ are emitted during arc welding processes.
 
• UV rays can cause eye damage, commonly referred to as "arc eye" or "welder's flash."
 
• Prolonged exposure to UV and IR rays may damage the skin and increase the risk of burns.
 
• Protective equipment such as welding helmets and gloves is essential to mitigate these hazards.
 
• IR rays are primarily responsible for thermal burns to the skin and eyes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Arc Welding Safety:**

 
 
• Always wear certified protective gear like welding helmets, safety goggles, gloves, and flame-resistant clothing.
 
• Ensure proper ventilation to avoid inhaling harmful fumes during welding.
 
 
 
• **Hazards of Other Rays:**
 
 
• X-rays and gamma rays are not emitted during arc welding but are used in industrial radiography.
 
• Microwaves and radio waves are unrelated to welding processes.
 
 
 
• **Importance of UV and IR Protection:**
 
 
• UV-blocking filters and heat-resistant materials in welding helmets provide critical protection against these rays.
 
• Failure to use proper protection can result in long-term health issues like cataracts or skin cancer.
